reviewContext.userProblem: Riela validates a sparse installed derived workflow as a complete workflow before resolving extends.workflowId, so documented user-scope Claude, Cursor, and Hydra variants cannot validate, inspect, or run against their installed base.
requiredOutcomes: A sparse derived workflow resolves its installed user-scope base before complete validation.
Validate, inspect, and deterministic run consume the same resolved derived bundle while ordinary workflows retain existing behavior.
String replacements, agent-node convenience patches, explicit node patches, caller instance patches, and caller run patches apply in the documented precedence order.
Focused Swift tests cover transformation precedence, installed derived CLI behavior, malformed or missing bases, direct and indirect cycles, and an ordinary workflow control.
The currently installed derived package passes deterministic validate, inspect, and run smoke checks with no real agent, command, add-on, commit, or push execution.
Implementation, independent reviews, broader verification, documentation and progress reconciliation, and exact commit/push evidence complete without performing the 0.1.39 release.
nonGoals: Do not redesign catalog selection, workflow provenance, or cross-workflow dispatch without a focused failing release-blocker test.
Do not perform the Riela 0.1.39 release, signing, notarization, or publication.
Do not add exhaustive inheritance conformance coverage or unrelated refactoring.
constraints: Keep production changes within the existing shared loader and resolver path plus the minimum representation needed for sparse extends declarations.
Resolve the required base through existing eligible user-scope installed-workflow lookup while preserving selection, activation, containment, package validation, and coordinated-read rules.
Preserve unrelated tracked and untracked work; use no worktrees, private implementation branches, concurrent Git operations, or shared-manifest worker edits.
Run foreground verification from the repository root, retain complete logs with terminal exit statuses under the evidence root, and serialize shared Swift build-directory use.
Use fresh reads, pre/post hashes, immutable intent evidence, worker-owned progress, serial reconciliation, and independent combined-tree review before finalization.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Recognize and validate the sparse inheritance declaration before ordinary complete decoding because manufacturing missing ordinary fields would hide the actual schema boundary.

Extend WorkflowRegistryBundleLoader.loadBundle with only base-resolution capability and active canonical-path/workflow-ID ancestry so validate, inspect, and run share one resolved bundle without a resolver redesign.
Use existing user-scope installed lookup and metadata-only inventory when workflow-ID discovery is needed to preserve established eligibility and package safety rules.
Recursively hydrate and validate the base, transform the materialized bundle in memory, validate each complete derived bundle, and retain derived source, scope, and package identity.

Apply literal replacements deterministically by descending UTF-8 source length then ascending UTF-8 bytes; patch originally file-backed agent nodes only; merge explicit node patches over convenience patches; apply caller patches once after inheritance.

Keep the tightly coupled declaration, transformation, loader, resolver, and CLI regression work in one implementation plan with ordered T1 through T4 waves; reserve shared indexes, documentation decisions, lockfiles, and broad formatting for serial reconciliation.
intentionalTradeoffs: One compact serial assignment limits merge and ownership risk at the cost of parallelism.
The patch supports the installed user-scope release blocker rather than a general inheritance resolver, favoring lower implementation and regression cost over completeness.
A small focused test set and one deterministic installed-package smoke replace an exhaustive scope and package matrix.
New helper files are optional bounded implementation locations, not required public abstractions; unused helpers should be omitted.
supportedEdgeCases: Malformed or null inheritance declarations, unknown inheritance keys, unsupported overlays, empty replacement sources, invalid patch shapes, unknown nodes, model-freeze violations, and transformation collisions fail with field-oriented diagnostics.
Missing installed bases identify derived and base IDs, searched user roots, and installation or scope guidance; selected invalid bases retain original file and field context.
Direct and indirect inheritance cycles are detected before recursive loading or lock reentry, and completed ancestry is removed so independent repeated base loads succeed.
Inherited prompt, command, and container resource paths remain usable without synthesizing replacement filenames or mutating either source bundle.
Convenience patches exclude shared nodeRef, add-on, command, and container nodes; explicit and caller patches retain documented precedence.
Workflows without extends continue through the ordinary strict validation path.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Exhaustive project, user, detached, mutable, and mixed scope-tier matrices.
Inheritance through --from-registry and generalized ambiguity policy expansion.
Generalized callee redesign or live cross-workflow machinery changes unless a focused failing installed-workflow regression proves the minimum repair is required.
Unrelated provenance abstractions, dependency changes, large-file splits, broad formatting, and speculative future-proofing.

acceptanceCriteria: A sparse derived workflow using extends validates from user scope when its installed base package is available.

The same derived workflow inspects and runs deterministically from the shared resolved bundle with derived identity, inherited steps, effective payloads, package identity, and exact mock output asserted.

Transformation precedence, malformed declarations, missing or invalid bases, direct and indirect cycles, repeated independent base loading, collisions, patch validation, and ordinary-workflow behavior have focused regression coverage.

The actual installed Claude derived package passes deterministic validate, inspect, and planning-only run smoke assertions with complete scenario coverage, unchanged installed bytes, and unchanged repository state.
Focused tests, the ordinary control, Swift build, RielaCoreTests and RielaCLITests, SwiftLint, and whitespace verification finish with complete logs and terminal exit statuses.
Implementation, test-integrity, adversarial, and combined-tree reviews leave no unresolved high or mid finding; documentation and progress state are reconciled serially.
Final commit and push evidence record matching hashes and exact files; the 0.1.39 release remains excluded.

Any shared-path production expansion is justified first by a retained focused failing blocker test, while shared indexes, documentation decisions, lockfiles, and broad formatting are edited only during serial reconciliation.
